Samir Patel: Quick announce — we're rolling out a preview of private-readonly-mode for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments :lock: 
Samir Patel: What it does: timeboxed 'freeze' that prevents operator-initiated config/model/agent changes during an audit or customer-specified window. Customer-admins can still read telemetry and export signed audit bundles.
Samir Patel: Why: customers asked for a simple, provable way to stop runtime drift while an auditor or compliance window is open. This reduces accidental/insider changes during attestation.
Samir Patel: Rollout plan: staging next Tue (pk-staging-3), limited previews by invite in 2 weeks, GA targeted ~6 weeks after preview depending on feedback.
Samir Patel: How to try (CLI):
Samir Patel: ```
# enable a 30-day readonly window for tenant t-0123
redwoodctl private enable-readonly --tenant t-0123 --duration 720h --reason "SOC2-audit"
# check status
redwoodctl private readonly-status --tenant t-0123
```
Samir Patel: Notes: read-only blocks: deploys, canary rollouts, config edits, agent upgrades initiated from Control Plane. It does NOT block customer-initiated actions taken inside their VPC (e.g., customer-managed KMS key rotations or image swaps) unless they also toggle the tenant-level enforcement.
Cleo Rivera: Nice. Does it automatically produce an audit artifact we can hand to customers?
Samir Patel: Yes — we generate a signed, append-only audit bundle for the freeze window (SHA256-signed, retention policy configurable). Export targets: S3/GCS/Azure Blob or local SCP.
Tariq Hassan: Any access model changes for support/ops? How does Support get emergency access if customer needs a hotfix during a freeze?
Elaine Chung: Good Q. We added an "emergency-unfreeze" flow that requires a two-person approval from the customer's admin + Redwood SOC on call. All emergency unfreeze events are recorded into the audit bundle. We'll publish the approval workflow in the runbook.
Samir Patel: Implementation detail: readonly mode flips a per-tenant enforcement flag in the Private control plane. Control plane refuses relevant APIs and adds a header X-ReadOnly-Active to rejected calls for easier tracing.
Samir Patel: Security note: because some customers run air-gapped setups, the enforcement model supports an offline approval token exchange (signed JWT) so SOC can authorize an emergency unfreeze without outbound calls.
Product Ops: Required step for customers: sign the "Freeze Window Addendum" in the contract portal. Preview invites will be sent to existing account contacts.
Oncall Bot: DeployBot: rollout started to cluster pk-staging-3 at 2026-03-23T15:02:11Z — job id db-7743.
Samir Patel: If you're on the preview list and want a demo, ping me or @Product Ops. We'll coordinate a quick sandbox session and share the runbook + CLI cheatsheet.
Cleo Rivera: Small UX ask — can we expose current readonly status in the Console header? Customers want a visible banner.
Samir Patel: Yes, that's in the preview UI patch (will show banner + reason + remaining time).
Tariq Hassan: For SRE: make sure canary rollback paths handle a readonly tenant (they should be NOPs). I'll add a check to the release checklist.
Elaine Chung: Documentation: drafting an internal runbook + customer-facing FAQ. Expect first drafts by EOD Fri.
Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. Big ask — if you spot any edge cases (especially around KMS, agent lifecycle, or on-prem orchestration), drop them here or open a ticket with label private-readonly-preview.
Product Ops: Preview invites + contract addendum links go out tomorrow 09:00 PT. :calendar: 
Samir Patel: cc @security for awareness.
